name: contextra-env
crate_doc: Canonical environment abstractions for Contextra (Clock, Rng, IdGen, Metrics).
Zero internal workspace dependencies (E0 Foundation Micro-Core).
Pure standard library environment contracts and deterministic test doubles.

public_items.name: Clock
doc: Port trait for time operations, enabling deterministic testing by decoupling
system wall-clock and monotonic time sources.
In production, [`SystemClock`] provides access to the real OS clocks.
In unit tests or simulations, deterministic doubles like `ManualClock` can be substituted.

methods.name: now_unix_nanos
doc: Returns the current wall-clock time as nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.
Returns `0` if system time is before the epoch instead of panicking.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-TIME-1`: Garantiert panikfrei; liefert bei Zeiten vor Unix-Epoche `0`.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei, liefert bei Zeit vor Unix-Epoche `0`.
# Crash
Reiner Statusabruf ohne persistente Mutation.

methods.name: monotonic_nanos
doc: Returns nanoseconds elapsed since a monotonic baseline reference point.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-TIME-2`: Garantiert panikfrei und monoton nicht fallend innerhalb des Prozesses.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei und monoton nicht fallend.
# Crash
Reiner Statusabruf ohne persistente Mutation.

public_items.name: SystemClock
doc: Standard production implementation of [`Clock`] backed by [`SystemTime`] and [`Instant`].

methods.name: new
doc: Creates a new [`SystemClock`] using the current [`Instant`] as the monotonic baseline.
# Didaktischer Hinweis
Die Initialisierung von `start_instant` via `Instant::now()` setzt einen unveränderlichen
Nullpunkt für die Berechnung von relativen Nanosekunden im Prozessleben.

public_items.name: prelude
doc: Prelude for environment ports.
Exports the four essential port traits required to build injectable components:
- [`Clock`]: Time operations
- [`Rng`]: Pseudorandom number generation
- [`IdGen`]: Monotonic and unique ID generation
- [`MetricsSink`]: Observability and telemetry

public_items.name: IdGen
doc: Port trait for unique ID generation.

methods.name: next_id
doc: Generates and returns the next unique 64-bit unsigned identifier.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-ID-1`: Keine Duplikate bei aufeinanderfolgenden Aufrufen; threadsichere Monotonie.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei durch atomare Operationen.
# Crash
Reiner flüchtiger RAM-Zustand; bei Crash wird der Generator neu initialisiert.

public_items.name: SequentialIdGen
doc: A thread-safe ID generator that produces monotonically increasing 64-bit IDs.
Wraps around safely on integer overflow (`u64::MAX` -> `0`) via atomic standard wrapping.

methods.name: new
doc: Creates a new [`SequentialIdGen`] starting at `start`.

public_items.name: unix_ms
doc: Converts clock time to unix milliseconds by rounding down (SPEC-v2 §4.2, B02).
Ensures deterministic millisecond calculation across legacy sub-crates
(`text`, `graph`, `vector`) by enforcing standard truncation integer division.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei, da [`Clock::now_unix_nanos`] stets einen `u64` liefert.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-TIME-1`: Bei Zeiten vor der Epoche liefert `now_unix_nanos()` 0, somit auch `unix_ms()` 0.

public_items.name: ManualClock
doc: Controllable clock implementation for testing determinism and time regression.
Permits precise manual stepping of unix and monotonic nanoseconds via atomic operations.

public_items.name: Rng
doc: Port trait for random number generators, enabling deterministic testing by decoupling
non-deterministic entropy sources.

methods.name: next_u64
doc: Generates the next pseudorandom 64-bit unsigned integer.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-RNG-1`: Deterministische Reproduzierbarkeit bei gleichem Seed.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei und nicht-blockierend.
# Crash
Reiner flüchtiger RAM-Zustand; bei Crash wird der Generator neu initialisiert.

methods.name: fill_bytes
doc: Fills `dest` with pseudorandom bytes generated by this RNG.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei für alle Puffergrößen.
# Crash
Reiner flüchtiger RAM-Zustand; keine persistente Mutation.

methods.name: next_unit_f64
doc: Returns a pseudorandom `f64` value in the half-open interval `[0.0, 1.0)`
with 53 bits of precision.
# Invarianten
- `INV-ENV-RNG-2`: Ergebnis liegt strikt im Bereich `[0.0, 1.0)`.
# Fehler
Keine; garantiert panikfrei.
# Crash
Reiner Statusabruf ohne persistente Mutation.

public_items.name: SeededRng
doc: A fast, deterministic 64-bit pseudorandom number generator using SplitMix64
with atomic state transitions (`AtomicU64`).
Lock-free and thread-safe without requiring `Mutex`.
# Entropy Seeding
Note that non-deterministic entropy seeding (e.g., via `OsRng` or system entropy)
is the responsibility of the Composition Root. Application entry points should gather entropy
at startup and pass the initial seed to [`SeededRng::new`].

methods.name: new
doc: Creates a new [`SeededRng`] initialized with the given seed.
Garantiert exakte Bitgleichheit zu den kanonischen Golden-Testvektoren.

methods.name: from_entropy
doc: Creates a new [`SeededRng`] seeded from process/runtime entropy.
# Non-Cryptographic Usage
This entropy source uses [`std::collections::hash_map::RandomState`] and an internal counter.
It is intended strictly for non-cryptographic usages such as jitter, load balancing,
and randomized algorithm initialization. Cryptographic keys and salts MUST use
dedicated cryptographic RNGs (`OsRng`).
# Composition Root Architecture
Only Composition Roots (application entry points) should construct a [`SeededRng`] via `from_entropy`.
Internal library logic MUST accept an injected [`Rng`] instance instead of calling `from_entropy` directly.
